source.description:
We're under-using bd's full command surface. Triage and skill docs only reference a small subset (mostly bd ready, bd create, bd dep add, bd close), leaving the richer relationship vocabulary and query/decision/epic features invisible to agents and humans.

## Specific gaps

### Relationship types (bd dep add --type ...)
The full list — almost none of which appear in skills or CLAUDE.md:
- blocks (default) — hard dependency, gates ready state
- tracks — follows another issue's progress without blocking
- related / relates-to — non-blocking 'see also' link (also bd dep relate)
- parent-child — epic/child structural edge (set automatically by bd create --parent)
- discovered-from — follow-up issue spawned during work on another
- until — time/condition-bound link
- caused-by — bug caused by another issue (root-cause link)
- validates — issue verifies/proves another (e.g. test validates feature)
- supersedes — replaces an older issue

### Likely under-used commands
- bd query — SQL-like compound filters (only briefly mentioned in CLAUDE.md)
- bd decision — record/list/manage architectural decisions with rationale
- bd epic — epic management subcommands beyond --parent
- bd compact / bd restore — semantic summarization of old closed issues
- bd audit — append-only JSONL agent-interaction log
- bd label — label management
- bd preflight --check — pre-PR readiness gate
- bd kv get/list — beyond memory-acked usage
- bd dep relate / --blocks shorthand vs --type forms

## Where to surface

1. **Triage skill (planned, see prior session)** — when building the bead-triager, it should USE the right relationship types automatically:
   - caused-by for bug → root-cause edges
   - discovered-from when spawning follow-ups during triage
   - supersedes when merging duplicates
   - validates when linking test issues to features
   - tracks for non-blocking 'watch this' links
   Without these, the triager will default to blocks/relates-to and lose semantic richness.

2. **using-xtrm skill** — add a 'Relationship vocabulary' section + a one-screen cheat-sheet of high-value bd commands beyond the basics (query, decision, preflight, audit, epic, compact).

3. **using-specialists / using-specialists-v3 skills** — clarify which relationship type to use when chaining specialist beads:
   - executor → reviewer: blocks (reviewer can't run until executor waits) or tracks?
   - debugger root-cause findings → fix bead: caused-by
   - follow-ups spawned during a specialist run: discovered-from
   - test bead ↔ impl bead: validates

4. **CLAUDE.md** — expand the bd Command Reference block with --type table + brief note on bd query/decision/preflight.

## Deliverables
- Cheat-sheet section in using-xtrm SKILL.md
- Relationship-type mapping section in using-specialists-v3 SKILL.md  
- Triage skill design must reference the relationship vocabulary explicitly
- CLAUDE.md bd reference expanded

## Why
Agents (and the operator) default to a 3-verb subset of bd. The dep graph stays semantically thin — every edge is 'blocks' even when 'caused-by' / 'validates' / 'supersedes' would carry more meaning for future triage and reporting. Fixing the docs is the cheapest leverage to upgrade every future session.

## Related
- Prior session: bead-triager skill idea (not yet filed as issue)
- ~/dev/specialists#unitAI-ylphl — workflow catalog epic (these conventions should reference the relationship vocabulary too)
